- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 79.16 → 81.20+), then undercorrects, leading to persistent overprediction.
- Underestimates in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days of 30d), suggesting model fails to capture late-stage mean reversion or policy-driven corrections.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days for most periods, indicating delayed reaction to new data or policy signals.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent spikes (e.g., 79.16–82.31), suggesting failure to adjust for volatility decay.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model holds prices too high for extended periods, failing to reflect natural downward drift after peaks.
- Forecasting horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are overly optimistic in early days, then overly pessimistic in late days, suggesting model lacks adaptive weighting for time decay.
